title: Mlai senior domain transfer learning
question: When does transfer learning actually help, and what can go wrong if you apply it carelessly?
idealAnswer:
Transfer learning helps most when the target task has limited labeled data but is related enough to the source task or domain that the pretrained representations, e.g. low-level visual features or general language understanding, are relevant

Fine-tuning strategy matters, freezing early layers and only fine-tuning later layers is often better with very little target data, since early layers tend to capture generic features while later layers are more task-specific

Catastrophic forgetting is a real risk, aggressive fine-tuning on a small target dataset can overwrite the useful general knowledge the pretrained model had, especially with too high a learning rate

If the source and target domains are too dissimilar, e.g. transferring a model pretrained on natural photos to medical X-rays, the pretrained features may not transfer well and can even hurt versus training from scratch

A strong answer mentions practical signals for when to use it, a small target dataset, a related domain, and limited compute or time to train from scratch
